title: Isolate edge-onprem TFState for GPU attachments and narrow IAM scopes
author: Priya Srinivasan
body:
Summary:
This PR introduces a set of Terraform module and state-layout changes to support edge/on-prem Private deployments where GPU nodepools are created and managed by tenant-bound controllers. The goal is to reduce blast radius during changes, enable safe per-edge tfstate checkpoints, and tighten IAM scopes for GPU attach/detach and subnet claims.

Motivation and context:
- Operators deploying Redwood Private into edge racks requested stronger isolation between tenant-managed GPU attachments and cluster-wide networking resources to avoid a single tfstate mutation impacting unrelated tenants.
- Existing monolithic tfstate for private clusters makes upgrades and rollbacks risky in environments with intermittent connectivity and manual approvals.
- Security review flagged overly-broad instance profile/POLICY attachments used by the GPU lifecycle controller; we need narrower IAM roles scoped by edge region and lease ID.

What changed (high level):
1) New modules added under modules/edge:
   - modules/edge/tfstate-anchor: helper that creates a namespaced backend key prefix and optional checksum tag for migration tooling.
   - modules/edge/edge-gpu-attach: idempotent GPU attach/detach resources, uses a delegated role and does not mutate cluster-level subnets.
   - modules/edge/iam-edge-lease: template for per-lease IAM role with assume-role conditions and minimum necessary permissions.
   - modules/edge/network-attachment-shard: lightweight network attachment resources that only hold minimal mapping data and DNS records.
2) Refactor of top-level private deployment layout to place edge attachments under their own tfstate prefixes (configurable by var.edge_tfstate_prefix).
3) Migration shim: scripts/migrate-edge-state.sh and a small terraform provider wrapper to create an initial anchor file and copy state entries into the new prefix with checksums.
4) Helm values: small values.yaml tweak to point the GPU lifecycle controller to the delegated role ARN and to a /metrics endpoint used by the migration job.

Design notes and constraints:
- The tfstate-anchor module purposely keeps state keys tiny and deterministic; it stores a single metadata key per edge that the migrator uses to validate copy/rename operations.
- The iam-edge-lease module restricts permissions to ec2:AttachVolume, ec2:DetachVolume, ec2:DescribeInstances, and iam:PassRole for a single role name pattern; it also scopes by aws:ResourceTag/edge-lease-id when available.
- Network-attachment-shard avoids creating or deleting VPCs: it only creates small route53 records and an attachment mapping resource consumed by the controller.
- The migration script is opinionated: it will transact copies into the new prefix and then mark the anchor as migrated. It can be NO-OPed with --dry-run.

Rollback and upgrade plan:
- We added a migration guard which requires that a successful plan and apply are recorded in the anchor metadata before the controller starts using the new state prefix.
- On failure, the controller retains the old state key and we include a revert path in scripts/migrate-edge-state.sh that will re-copy the original keys back.

Testing and validation performed:
- Unit-style validation: terraform validate on all modules and fmt/lint fixes.
- Integration: ran the migration in a staging edge cluster with three tenant leases, validated controller reconciliations, and simulated a failover where control plane connectivity dropped and came back.
- Security: verified IAM role policies in a dry-run account and ensured no wildcard resource ARNs beyond the necessary instance profiles.
- Performance: confirmed that moving to smaller per-lease state prefixes reduces plan time by ~28% in a 1200-resource state snapshot.

Commits included (summary):
- 1) add edge tfstate-anchor and helper scripts (migrate-edge-state.sh, README)
- 2) introduce edge-gpu-attach, iam-edge-lease, network-attachment-shard modules and document expected usage
- 3) refactor root private layout to accept var.edge_tfstate_prefix and wire delegated role ARNs into values.yaml and examples
- 4) tests: add local integration harness script and add CI lint rule exceptions for the migration scripts

Files changed (high-level):
- modules/edge/tfstate-anchor/main.tf, outputs.tf, README.md
- modules/edge/edge-gpu-attach/{main.tf,variables.tf,iam.tpl}
- modules/edge/iam-edge-lease/{policy.json.tpl,main.tf}
- modules/edge/network-attachment-shard/{main.tf,outputs.tf}
- examples/private/edge-deploy/values.yaml (helm values reference)
- scripts/migrate-edge-state.sh (bash, idempotent)
- README-private-edge.md (migration and rollout documentation)
- tests/integration/edge-migration-ci.yml (CI harness changes)

Small illustrative snippet (edge-gpu-attach/main.tf):
resource "aws_iam_role" "edge_lease_role" {
  name = format("redwood-edge-lease-%s-%s", var.edge_id, var.lease_id)
  assume_role_policy = data.template_file.assume_role.rendered
  tags = { "edge-lease-id" = var.lease_id }
}

Review conversation (abridged into this single body string):
- Liam O'Connor: "Great direction. Two asks: 1) can we avoid any drift windows where both tfstate prefixes are writable? 2) add a rollout checklist for support to follow during live migrations."
- Priya (author): "Answer: migration is copy-only until the anchor is flipped; copy uses object-level checksum verification to avoid partial moves. Added a rollout checklist to README-private-edge.md and a dry-run flag to the script."
- Diego Morales: "IAM template looks good but please run tfsec/opa scans; also consider limiting iam:PassRole to specific role ARNs instead of pattern where reachable."
- Priya: "Addressed: tightened PassRole to specific naming pattern and added tfsec suppressions where the provider forces dynamic names; added CI step to run tfsec on modules/edge."
- Zara Patel: "Minor: docs should call out expected RBAC for the controller pod; otherwise LGTM."
- Final: Approved by reviewers after the tfsec fix and doc addition.

CI and checks:
- terraform fmt/lint: pass
- unit-validate: pass
- tfsec security scan: initially failed (rule AWS018 - iam_passrole_wildcard) on commit 2, fixed in commit 3, rerun passed
- integration/edge-migration-ci: pass (ran a small staging migration)

Release notes (for operators):
- Introduces per-edge tfstate prefixing and new edge modules for GPU attachments and IAM lease roles.
- Migration tooling included; operators must run scripts/migrate-edge-state.sh per edge before upgrading controllers to v1.7.0.

Why this is different from earlier state refactors:
- Prior PRs reorganized large tfstate boundaries for multi-tenant clouds; this PR targets low-connectivity edge/on-prem installations and introduces a small-footprint anchor + copy-based migrator that is safe for manually operated environments.

Merge outcome:
- Squash-merged to main once CI green and approvals obtained. The migration guide and scripts were included in the merge commit.

Followups planned:
- Add a controller-side feature flag to allow automatic switching to the new state prefix after a configurable grace period (ENG-2189).
- Add metrics to track migration success/failure per-edge (ENG-2201).

If you need to reproduce the migration in staging: see README-private-edge.md -> "Migration quickstart" which lists required IAM, S3 backend access, and the dry-run command.
